messages:
siva: Heads-up — I see a regression in multi-GPU throughput after the recent kernel-selection heuristic change. Small-step pipeline runs are showing ~18% lower token/sec when mixed TP+PP is active.
jenna: ugh, when did that land? any obvious stack traces or perf profiles?
siva: landed in deploy 2101, kernelselect v2. The interesting bit: all-reduce time spikes for tiny grad sizes (~<4KB) and stalls overlap with KV cache prefetch on some nodes.
mike: do you have profiler dumps? timeline helps.
siva: pasted a condensed timeline below (from perf-trace):

```
[time 0.00s] forward microbatch 0 start
[time 0.07s] allreduce start (0.002s)  <-- small-grad allreduce
[time 0.09s] kv-prefetch hit
[time 0.18s] compute resume
[time 0.32s] backend kernelselect switch -> fallback path
[time 0.50s] stall waiting on p2p (nvlink->pcie hop)
```

and a quick flame summary: comm edges dominate on some ranks, compute edges fragmented.
andrea: NVLink/PCIe mixed-rack scheduling? sounds like topology-aware routing isn't picking the fast path. Are we falling back to ring instead of hierarchical allreduce?
siva: exactly — kernelselect changed preferred algorithm to NCCL ring for small messages to avoid kernel launch overhead, but on mixed-topology that leads to cross-hop traffic instead of using NVLink local host reduces. Result: more PCIe<->EFA crossing.
jenna: that explains it. So two knobs to try: (1) prefer hierarchical/allreduce-tree when topology indicates NVLink clusters, (2) raise the small-msg threshold so tiny grads use p2p rendezvous instead of ring, (3) tweak KV cache prefetch to avoid kicking off large DMA during critical comm windows.
mike: I ran a quick sim on 8xA100 where 4 GPUs are NVLink-paired and 4 are PCIe-only. Switching to hierarchical reduced cross-host traffic by ~40% and improved overlap.
perf-bot: perf snapshot uploaded: https://perf.redwood/shot/2105556789-1 (flame, timeline, p2p-latency CSV). :thumbsup:
andrea: can we repro reliably? we need a small e2e CI job that toggles kernelselect and topology hints. If CI reproduces, add rollback or an emergency flag in kernelselect.
siva: I can add a reduced repro config: --microbatches 4 --tp-size 2 --pp-size 2 --kv-prefetch async. Will run on the mixed fabric cluster tonight and post traces.
jenna: also let's add a probe that samples per-allreduce path selection and p2p latencies in the runtime tracing. Right now metrics are too coarse.
mike: +1. I'll add a quickly-rolled probe to measure per-allreduce hop count and mark any selection that crosses NIC boundary.
andrea: action items: siva run repro + perf dump (ETA tonight). mike add hop-count probe (tomorrow). jenna prepare rollout rollback flag and threshold config (EOD). I'll triage infra scheduling to force NVLink-local packing for the repro job.
siva: posting initial repro results in this thread when done. thanks.
perf-bot: automated note: the last deploy touching kernelselect was reverted once in canary on 2102 but re-promoted on 2104. See changelist CL#3456.
siva: noted — will include CL# in report.
jenna: if we can't get overlap back with heuristic tweaks, fallback plan is to disable the tiny-msg ring optimization by default until we implement topology-aware decisioning.
andrea: agree. prefer conservative default.
jenna: ok locking that as a config toggle so we can A/B test.
